title: Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC)
summary: Evaluate access from trusted subject, resource, action, and environment attributes when static roles cannot express the required business boundary.
overview: Attribute-based access control evaluates policy over properties of the requester, target resource, operation, and environment. An agent may read a document only if its tenant matches, its classification is permitted, the user's assignment is current, and the processing region is approved. These conditions can be expressed without creating a role for every combination.

The difficult part is attribute trust and freshness. A sophisticated policy is ineffective if the model supplies its own department, document classification, or approval status. Define authoritative attribute sources, missing-value behavior, policy versions, and the point at which a decision must be rechecked before execution.

production.poc: A prototype can model a few explicit predicates and test permit and deny examples. Include absent and conflicting attributes from the start.
production.production: Production separates policy decision from enforcement, authenticates attribute sources, and defaults safely when required facts are unavailable. Bind decisions to the exact resource and action.
production.scale: At scale, cache decisions only with bounded validity and relevant attribute versions. Analyze policy conflicts and latency because repeated remote lookups can become a critical-path dependency.

components.name: Attribute authorities
components.role: Supply verified user, resource, tenant, classification, and environmental facts.

components.name: Policy decision point
components.role: Evaluates versioned rules and returns allow, deny, or a defined indeterminate result.

components.name: Policy enforcement point
components.role: Blocks the actual data or tool operation unless the decision permits it.

components.name: Policy administration
components.role: Reviews, tests, versions, and deploys access rules.

components.name: Decision audit
components.role: Records relevant attribute provenance and policy results without unnecessary sensitive payloads.

flow.title: Identify operation
flow.description: Establish the exact principal, resource, action, and execution environment.

flow.title: Fetch trusted attributes
flow.description: Resolve authoritative values and their freshness rather than accepting prompt assertions.

flow.title: Evaluate policy
flow.description: Apply explicit combining rules, missing-value handling, and any required obligations.

flow.title: Bind decision
flow.description: Associate the result with resource version, action parameters, and a limited validity interval.

flow.title: Enforce operation
flow.description: Recheck changed critical attributes before consequential execution and apply required constraints.

flow.title: Record evidence
flow.description: Store policy version, decision, and attribute provenance for review and incident analysis.

useCase.title: Restricting access to engineering records
useCase.situation: An aerospace supplier shares engineering documents across programs, contractors, and processing regions.
useCase.problem: A broad engineer role cannot express project membership, document classification, contract expiry, and permitted region together.
useCase.requirement: The assistant must retrieve only engineering evidence allowed for the specific person and current assignment.
useCase.architecture: Trusted directories and document metadata feed a policy engine that evaluates each retrieval and document download.
runtime: A contractor asks about a component tolerance; the retrieval service checks active program membership and document attributes before exposing the passage.
Opening the cited drawing triggers another check against the current contract and resource version.
useCase.failure: If classification metadata is missing, the document remains unavailable until the owner repairs it; the agent cannot infer a lower classification.
useCase.impact: Measure indeterminate decisions, attribute freshness, policy latency, and denied cross-program access. Policy design must be reviewed by the organization's access-control owners.

tradeoffs.benefit: Complex boundaries can be represented without thousands of roles.
tradeoffs.cost: Attribute ownership and policy debugging become harder.

tradeoffs.benefit: Consistent decisions can span retrieval and tools.

tradeoffs.cost: Stale attributes can preserve access after conditions change.

failures.scenario: User-controlled metadata becomes an authority attribute
failures.detection: Provenance validation identifies an untrusted source.
failures.recovery: Reject the value and resolve it from the approved authority.

failures.scenario: Policy changes between review and execution
failures.detection: Bound decision version or resource state no longer matches.

mistakes.mistake: Allowing missing attributes to match permissive defaults
mistakes.fix: Define explicit indeterminate and deny behavior.
Include resource, action, relevant versions, and validity bounds.
Evaluate them in a deterministic policy service.

whenToUse: Access depends on resource and environmental context.
Tenant and classification rules cut across organizational roles.
Trusted attribute sources and policy ownership exist.
whenNotToUse: Simple stable roles fully express the required permissions.
Critical attributes have no trustworthy source.
The team cannot test or explain policy interactions.
checklist: Name an authority for every attribute.
Define missing and conflicting value behavior.
Measure decision latency and indeterminate rates.
